title: Conversion Stage Is Not Outcome
summary: An eight-question map for locating named project and adoption evidence without treating unlike stages as a common maturity scale or a later operating outcome.
map_question: Which distinct evidence questions separate named context from authority, commitment, implementation, validation, acceptance, recurring operation, and comparable outcomes?
interpretation_boundary: The stages are shared questions, not a universal legal or technical sequence. The map does not rank files, equate unlike systems, create a readiness score, or allow an upstream event to prove a downstream stage.

nodes.label: 1. Named context
nodes.note: Preserve the exact entity, place, institution, operator, and evidence boundary before reading movement.

nodes.label: 2. Policy or authority
nodes.note: A policy, permit, regulatory decision, or service authority is real but remains upstream of implementation and acceptance.

nodes.label: 3. Finance, procurement, or agreement
nodes.note: A financial close, order, contract, or delivery agreement establishes commitment without proving delivery.

nodes.label: 4. Build or implementation
nodes.note: Physical construction or system implementation must stay tied to the named entity and exact scope.

nodes.label: 5. Test, compliance, or qualification
nodes.note: Inspection, testing, compliance, qualification, and corrective action require their own accepted artifacts.

nodes.label: 6. Accepted service, product, or cutover
nodes.note: A receiving authority or customer must accept the defined asset, service, product, or transition.

nodes.label: 7. Recurring operation or output
nodes.note: One acceptance or bounded claim does not establish compatible recurring operation.

nodes.label: 8. Comparable outcome
nodes.note: A bounded outcome needs stable identity, period, definition, method, denominator, and acceptance.

nodes.label: No automatic stage transfer
nodes.note: Each cell answers one question only; evidence does not flow forward automatically or sideways into another entity.

links.note: Authority can be interpreted only after the entity and scope are stable; some files enter through a different stage.
Authority and commitment are separate questions and may occur in different orders.
A commitment does not itself establish build or implementation.
Implementation remains distinct from test, compliance, qualification, and corrective action.
Testing or compliance does not prove receiving-system acceptance.
One accepted event does not establish recurring operation or output.
Repeated activity still needs stable definitions, denominators, and outcome measures.
The no-transfer boundary prevents upstream, adjacent, or incompatible evidence from becoming an outcome claim.

what_this_map_supports: Eight named files can be asked the same evidence questions while retaining different legal, technical, and commercial paths.
Evidence Present, Partial / Held, and Not Established are bounded cell labels rather than numeric measures.
The next decisive artifact can target one open stage without implying every earlier or later stage is complete.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not rank files or compare maturity, readiness, value, risk, safety, or performance.
It does not imply a universal sequence or that unlike cell states are technically equivalent.
It does not convert authority, commitment, build, testing, acceptance, or repeated activity into a comparable outcome.
next_records_needed: Accepted infrastructure, qualification, service, product, or cutover records tied to the named entity.
Compatible recurring operation or output with stable identity and period.
Repeated outcome records with stable definitions, methods, denominators, and receiving-system acceptance.
